A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite v3's changed title and substantially expanded formulation. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and shared methods and results can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-32 generation experiments, FID measurements, path-optimization results, and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original synthetic transportation and image-generation experiments, including conditional generation, joint optimization, and supplementary analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: v2 optimizes a Fourier path network while freezing the SI model. v3 adds joint vector-field/MAC adversarial optimization and optional reuse of conventional pretrained checkpoints. It also revises coefficient sampling and sinusoidal parameterization and introduces inference updates using coefficient increments (Section 3; Appendices C–D). These change training and inference beyond renaming tensor-valued time.

E1.justification: v3 retains CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-32 and adds synthetic transportation among Gaussian, eight-Gaussian, and moons distributions, FFHQ and AFHQv2 image generation, and class-conditional CIFAR-10 and ImageNet generation. This substantially broadens the represented distributions, domains, and task requirements beyond v2's image-generation coverage.

E2.justification: v2 primarily compares scalar/tensor variants of SI, FM, and DDPM. v3 Table 5 adds comparisons with EDM, CTM, consistency models, rectified-flow variants, and StyleGAN models, explicitly computing CTM results at five and six NFE. Conversely, the modified scalar-conditioning comparators in v2 Table 7 disappear from the corresponding v3 Table 10.

E3.justification: v3 introduces random-versus-OT pairing controls, additional optimized NFE settings, five-NFE EDM experiments, and separate 500k-image ablation and 1.5M-image main CIFAR-10 training budgets. It adds FDDINOv2 and explicitly accounts for MAC computation with '(+)' NFE notation. Appendix F reports EDM/EDM2 evaluation software where v2 specifies PyTorch-FID; the 50,000 generated evaluation samples are retained.

E4.justification: Conditioning, coefficient range, filtering, and dimensionality were already analyzed in v2. v3 extends these investigations and adds model-only, MAC-only, and joint-training controls (Table 6), learned-coefficient t-SNE analysis (Figure 8), and measured deviation from linear trajectories (Appendix E.3.3). These substantially strengthen analysis of what MAC contributes.

E5.justification: v2 reports the minimum of three FID calculations and mentions approximate random variation. v3 retains minimum-of-three image-metric reporting and explicitly mentions different seeds. Its new synthetic experiments report means and standard deviations over three separately trained seeds (Table 1; Appendix E.1.2). This is a localized uncertainty-reporting addition, without establishing increased image-training repetitions.

E6.justification: The optimized SI FIDs of 4.14 on CIFAR-10 and 7.06 on ImageNet-32 reappear, alongside many retained scalar-model results. However, v3 revises DDPM entries and adds extensive transportation, benchmark, and ablation results. Table 5 newly reports conditional CIFAR-10 FID 1.37 and ImageNet-64 FID 1.48/FDDINOv2 70.2. These are newly reported outcomes under expanded methods and settings, not same-setting gains over v2.

T1.justification: v2 presents SI definitions and a transport/score theorem. v3 introduces formal matrix-valued coefficients and trajectory-conditioned MAC definitions, explicit coefficient hypothesis sets, and separate fixed-field and joint optimization objectives. Appendix D adds a derivation using finite coefficient increments. This substantially revises the mathematical formulation rather than merely changing notation.

C1.justification: v3 retains adaptive multidimensional path optimization but broadens the contribution from tensor-valued training and frozen-SI path optimization to a plug-in across flow/diffusion frameworks with joint model/trajectory training and optional checkpoint reuse. It newly claims substantial adversarial-training efficiency and state-of-the-art conditional CIFAR-10 generation.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations that nonstraight trajectories can improve transportation even with OT-trained fields and that class conditioning can dominate initial-noise dependence in learned coefficients. It also argues for compatibility without coefficient pretraining. v2's DDPM curvature-based failure explanation is dropped, while fixed-NFE and VRAM constraints remain discussed within future directions and training efficiency.

D1.justification: Much of v2 Appendix B's architecture and training information is retained in v3 Appendix E.2. v3 additionally documents synthetic-model configurations, coefficient filtering/padding/rescaling, EDM time schedules and conditioning, separate optimization hyperparameters, dropout handling, GPU configurations, and training times (Appendices C–E; Tables 14–15). These materially expand reproducibility information for the revised procedures.

R1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites research positioning around trajectory optimality and diffusion distillation, adding discussion of CTM, consistency and distribution-matching methods, neural flow diffusion, and newer trajectory methods. It explicitly distinguishes joint inference-plan/vector-field optimization from distillation. This replaces much of v2's broader CNF/flow/diffusion survey and changes the novelty argument.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction, related work, and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten around MAC. Framework background moves into Appendix A, experiments are reorganized into synthetic, image MAC-only, and joint-optimization sections, and appendices expand from A–C to A–G. The change is extensive rewriting and restructuring, beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 switches the main text to two columns and substantially redesigns its illustrations and result displays: new trajectory schematics, grouped benchmark tables, training curves, t-SNE plots, and paired baseline/MAC sample grids replace or supplement v2's displays. Some existing tables are relocated and expanded. Figure 12's FFHQ/AFHQ score assignments conflict with Table 5.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v2's limited validation of optimized paths, previously centered on SI and 32×32 images. Comparisons with strong methods, experiments across additional frameworks and conditional tasks, and controls separating MAC from model adversarial training provide much stronger evidence for the contribution. Expanded implementation details and seeded synthetic results also improve assessability. The Figure 12/Table 5 labeling inconsistency and retained fixed-NFE limitation qualify, but do not outweigh, these substantial gains.
